title: 2026 landfill methane measurement and permit-monitoring QA controls

sources.title: Landfill operators: environmental permits - Monitor and report your performance

facts.source_fact: Environment Agency published the landfill methane measurement and metrics research on 2 February 2026.
facts.expected_handling: Carry the research publication date and regulator provenance with derived method controls.

facts.source_fact: The research assesses landfill methane measurement methods and considers how measurements could be used in regulation.
facts.expected_handling: Treat measurement outputs as method/regulatory evidence, not parcel values.

facts.source_fact: The research investigated two different measurement methods for demonstrating effectiveness of landfill gas management.
facts.expected_handling: Preserve method identity before comparing results.

facts.source_fact: The research found measurement could help improve landfill gas capture and reduce methane emissions.
facts.expected_handling: Record this as a research conclusion, not a quantified site reduction.

facts.source_fact: Landfill permit holders must monitor during site planning, operation and aftercare.
facts.expected_handling: Attach lifecycle phase to every monitoring record.

facts.source_fact: An emissions monitoring plan must accompany the permit application and requires Environment Agency approval.
facts.expected_handling: Reject unapproved monitoring-plan status as equivalent to permit-approved monitoring.

facts.source_fact: Monitoring design must consider background concentrations, measurement uncertainty and QA/QC including calibration, sample storage and audit trail.
facts.expected_handling: Require uncertainty and QA/QC metadata for monitored results.

facts.source_fact: Site-specific permit monitoring may include landfill gas, point-source emissions, groundwater, surface water, leachate and particulate matter.
facts.expected_handling: Do not infer a universal parameter list beyond permit scope.

facts.source_fact: Hazardous or non-hazardous landfill site preparation requires 12 background gas datasets representative of a 12-month period, including CH4, CO2, O2 and atmospheric pressure.
facts.expected_handling: Check background-series completeness before operational comparison.

facts.source_fact: Operational hazardous or non-hazardous landfills must monitor trace components in landfill gas for site-specific risk assessment and gas-management planning.
facts.expected_handling: Preserve trace-component composition and risk-assessment context.

facts.source_fact: Risk assessment must inform monitoring to identify uncontrolled emissions such as well heads, pipework, engines, flares and surface flux.
facts.expected_handling: Classify source type before aggregating emissions evidence.

facts.source_fact: Operators must monitor the efficiency of the landfill gas extraction system.
facts.expected_handling: Keep extraction-efficiency evidence separate from surface-flux measurements.

facts.source_fact: Monitoring data must be used to review the site's GasSim model every year.
facts.expected_handling: Carry model-review year and observed-data vintage together.

facts.source_fact: Cells that accepted biodegradable waste require a two-stage CH4 cap-emission approach: identify and fix containment/collection faults, then measure intact-cap CH4 flux at representative points.
facts.expected_handling: Require both survey/fault and representative-flux stages before treating cap monitoring as complete.

facts.source_fact: The Environment Agency surface standard for a permanently capped zone is an average CH4 flux of 0.001 mg/m2/second.
facts.expected_handling: Attach zone type and unit to any comparison with this standard.

facts.source_fact: The Environment Agency surface standard for a temporarily capped zone is an average CH4 flux of 0.1 mg/m2/second.
facts.expected_handling: Do not compare temporary-cap results against the permanent-cap standard.

facts.source_fact: Where a zone or feature exceeds the surface standard, the operator must review the gas management plan, reduce emissions, identify local sources, quantify them and remediate where necessary.
facts.expected_handling: Record exceedance response and remediation status.

facts.source_fact: High cap variability or high uncertainty in flux calculation requires an improved monitoring procedure for subsequent surveys.
facts.expected_handling: Escalate uncertain flux evidence instead of presenting it as precise.

facts.source_fact: Continuous monitoring data availability must be at least 95%; below this threshold the operator must investigate, prevent recurrence and estimate missing-period data and impact.
facts.expected_handling: Apply the 95% completeness gate before accepting continuous-monitoring summaries.

facts.source_fact: Annual reporting normally includes landfill-gas volumes combusted in engines, combusted in flares or used in other ways, with permit-specific reporting requirements.
facts.expected_handling: Keep utilisation route and reporting period explicit.

guard_patterns.handling: Preserve the cited source fact without broadening its scope.
Attach landfill type, permit scope, zone or monitoring phase before downstream use.
guard_patterns.risk_prevented: Prevents mixing incompatible landfill monitoring conditions.

guard_patterns.handling: Attach publication, monitoring and reporting dates and the applicable permit/model vintage.
Carry method, unit, uncertainty, QA/QC and source provenance into derived outputs.
Do not convert landfill method or permit evidence into a parcel-level measured emission without a separate parcel-binding gate.

generation_rule: CARTESIAN_PRODUCT facts x guard_patterns; control_id={package_id}_{fact_id}_{pattern_id}; each generated row inherits confidence_percent=99 and verification=PASS
